architecture.controlPlane: All providers are loaded by the generated lazy registry and execute through the tenant-scoped Connection Service, encrypted credential store, ACL/visibility checks, ConnectionLease, action policy, audit store, and catalog enablement.
architecture.credentialHandling: Only encrypted credential ciphertext is persisted. Profiles and action results are redacted. Runtime code does not call lark-cli, DingTalk CLI, browser sessions, or Studio-managed credentials.
architecture.egress: Provider egress uses the shared guarded fetch or explicit guarded endpoint validation. User-supplied source URLs remain public-only. Alibaba OSS SDK requests use a custom urllib adapter backed by the injected guarded fetch and bounded response reads.
architecture.boundedReads: Object downloads and sourceUrl ingestion use transit storage/readBoundedResponseBytes with abort cleanup. Office and object listing actions expose bounded pages or cursors. Office ResourceRef schema hints and DingTalk/WeCom directory action results are depth/item/field/size bounded and redact credential-like fields. Control-plane discovery and runtime actions require a ConnectionLease bound to the current connection revision. Successful discovery replaces a tenant/workspace/connection/revision-scoped ResourceRef allowlist; bound resource actions are rejected with resource_not_discovered before executor loading or provider egress when the ID/token is absent, stale, cross-tenant, or the discovered resource kind does not match. Required bindings reject missing values; optional bindings are checked only when supplied, including every string in array-valued bindings. Callers without the tenant authorizer fail closed. S3 and OSS discovery validates a configured bucket through the native provider path or uses bounded native bucket listing; TOS discovery validates and exposes only its configured bucket. Explicit storage bucket inputs are optional resource bindings, while omitted buckets use the connection default and remain provider-allowlist checked.
architecture.writePolicy: TOS exposes no write/delete/presign actions. Existing S3/OSS write actions remain catalog/runtime compatibility surfaces and require the existing control-plane lease to be explicitly scoped.
